sources.observed_relation: # Make den-edge's data plane bounded, streaming, and representation-first ## Goal Keep den-edge one self-contained Rust process with a tiny, hard-bounded footprint while making it scale vertically across the six physical cores available to it. There is deliberately no cluster, external database, cache service, or rendering fleet in this plan. The desired hot path serves or forwards bytes whose identity is already known. It should not repeatedly read, hash, parse, build a `serde_json::Value` tree, serialize, and compress the same representation. Cold and high-cardinality results remain on demand: we cannot prebuild 100k person pages, 50k title pages, every upstream object, or every `(library, generation, head, since, limit, encoding)` sync page. Prepared representations therefore mean only: - startup/build metadata for the finite web asset set; - canonical bodies plus validators for upstream objects fetched on demand; - indexed, serialization-friendly authoritative library state; - a very small, strictly byte-bounded in-memory cache for exact responses that prove hot; - bounded streaming for everything else.
